newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Prime to buy Golden West Network.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Prime to buy Golden West Network.

text.p: Prime Television Ltd said on Tuesday it had agreed to buy the Western Australian-based Golden West Network for A$71 million.
The company also said that its revenue in the first four months of 1996/97 was ahead of last year.

Prime said the purchase of Golden West Network (GWN) from Kerry Stokes' unlisted media group Australian Capital Equity would make it the largest regional television network in Australia. It said the purchase would be funded by a A$60 million debt facility from the Australia and New Zealand Banking Group Ltd and existing cash reserves.

"GWN has over 460,000 viewers in Western Australia. When added to our existing viewers in New South Wales, Victoria and southeast Queensland, this will boost Prime Television's national reach to some 4.4 million people," Prime chairman Paul Ramsay said.
Prime chief executive George Brown said in a statement that the company achieved higher sales and net profit in the first four months of 1996/97, but did not provide specific details.
While advertising markets had been flat for most of 1996, the Olympic Games had delivered significant extra revenue in July an August, he said.

"In the two months since the conclusion of the Olympics, sales have continued to exceed the 1995 results, although it is difficult to establish a clear trend. Profits for the four months are also ahead of the corresponding period in 1995," Brown said. -- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
